q: How much electricity can a vitrified tile polishing line save?
title: Tile polishing line: kWh saved by new motors
short: About a quarter, in BEE's Morbi report. Replacing the motors on one plant's grinding, calibration, polishing and sizing machines cut the line from 2,108,808 to 1,605,900 kWh a year: 502,908 kWh, roughly 340 t CO2 on today's grid. Cost Rs 25.79 lakh, payback 1.26 years at 2010 prices.
audience: Morbi and other vitrified tile plant owners whose polishing line takes 40 to 45% of the plant's electricity

sections.h: What the auditors found on the line
ul: Seven machines with 971 kW connected drew only 501 kW on average, so most motors ran below half load.
Average motor efficiency was about 70%; the replacement motors were rated at 86.4%.
The line ran 24 hours a day, 250 days a year, and used 1.37 to 2.28 kWh per square metre of tile across the units audited.
Motors cost Rs 20.21 lakh of the Rs 25.79 lakh total. Procurement and fitting: 4 weeks, done on days the line is idle.

sections.h: Where the saving comes from, machine by machine
ul: Polishing 2 (100 kW measured on 174 kW): 117,387 kWh a year.
Rough grinding (46 kW on 97 kW): 70,042 kWh.
Sizing (93 kW on 115 kW, the best loaded): 49,803 kWh.

sections.h: Why the report's 402 t CO2 is high
p: The report used an older grid factor of about 0.8 kg per kWh. On CEA's FY 2025-26 factor of 0.675, the same 502,908 kWh is about 339 t of CO2 a year. The kWh saving is the solid number; the CO2 follows the grid year you report.

ul: Log each machine's actual kW for a full shift with a clamp meter. Lightly loaded motors gain most; a well loaded one may not pay back.
Check whether a smaller motor, not only a more efficient one, fits each machine.
Fit a sub-meter on the polishing line first, so the before and after kWh come from the same meter.
Report kWh per square metre polished each month, not just total kWh, so a change in output does not hide the saving.

example.title: One plant's polishing line for a year
lines: At about 5,929 m2 a day for 250 days: roughly 1.42 kWh per m2 down to 1.08 (estimate)
example.note: Grid factor from CEA's database for FY 2025-26, an estimate. The square metre figures assume the report's suitable plant size; use your own output.

senseible: Senseible reads each electricity bill and gives monthly kWh and CO2 with the grid factor for that bill's year, so a drop after the motor change shows up in your records. The green loan check shows what a lender will ask for before funding it.
